page: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v7 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware cryptography instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an unusually high ratio of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, requiring attached remote storage for disk-based data persistence.

Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional single-threaded execution alongside standard multi-threaded throughput. In single-core tests, the server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng (3,631.57), single-threaded gzip compression (40.09 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.35 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded operations fall within average tiers due to the constrained 4-vCPU footprint, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 7,229.58, a PassMark CPU score of 9,726.66, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 33.34 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows average throughput, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 447.73 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads and writes attaining 46.95 GB/sec and 33.73 GB/sec, respectively.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the E16-4as_v7 is its heavily skewed memory-to-vCPU ratio. By restraining the compute allotment to 4 vCPUs while maintaining 128.0 GB of memory, the instance delivers high cost efficiency for workloads constrained by per-core database licensing rather than total compute capacity. In application benchmarks, it processes 7.77 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 8.55 GB/sec. However, raw CPU-heavy tasks such as prompt processing on medium-sized 7B LLM models rank low, recording 15.87 tokens/sec.

This hardware profile is tailored for memory-bound workloads that do not demand extensive core counts. Best-fit use cases include in-memory databases, Redis caches, licensed relational database management systems such as SQL Server or Oracle, and analytics caching layers requiring extensive memory residency.
